title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a short boxed fragment, and almost all of it is struck through. It is a draft of the standing hypotheses for the construction on the previous and next pages.

The previous page defines an O_S-linear map C~ : ω = f_*Ω^1_{X/S} → ω^{(p)}. This is the Cartier operator viewed as a semilinear map on global 1-forms, i.e. the Hasse–Witt/Cartier–Manin datum on H^0(Ω^1). Iterating it gives F_*^{(ν)} : ω → ω^{(p^ν)}. When λ ↦ λ^{p^ν} is the identity on O_S (e.g. S = Spec F_{p^ν}), this is an O_S-linear endomorphism of ω. Forms with C~ω = ω^{(p)}, which are locally logarithmic derivatives, are fixed by F_*^{(ν)}.

The next page realises F_*^{(ν)} as the trace Tr along the iterated relative Frobenius F^{(ν)}_{X/S} : X → X^{(p^ν/S)}. It uses duality for finite flat morphisms and notes that F^{(ν)}_{X/S}, composed with the canonical projection, equals F_X^ν.

This page tries to state the minimal hypotheses for that trace description. Read in modern terms:
- X is an S-scheme (S of characteristic p) such that the relative Frobenius F_{X/S} : X → X^{(p/S)} is flat and locally of finite presentation (with X → S locally of finite presentation). Then F_{X/S} is finite locally free, so a trace Tr_{F_{X/S}} : F_*Ω^1_X → Ω^1_{X^{(p)}} can be defined.
- The case 'X lisse sur S' is the basic instance ('plus généralement').
- Further attempted conditions concern the geometric fibres and Ω^1_{X/S} being locally free.

The whole box is crossed out. Grothendieck evidently abandoned the general formulation and returned, on the next page, to X/S smooth of relative dimension 1.
errors: No mathematical claim is completed, so there is nothing to check in detail.

The 'more general' hypothesis (F_{X/S} flat and lfp) is in fact essentially equivalent to smoothness when X → S is flat and lfp, by the relative Kunz theorem. So the intended generalisation is weaker than it might look; this may be why it was struck out.

ideas.what: Hypotheses making the relative Frobenius finite locally free so that the Cartier operator can be defined as a trace
ideas.modern_name: Relative Frobenius finite flat; Cartier operator as trace / Grothendieck duality for finite flat morphisms

ideas.what: Flatness of relative Frobenius as a generalisation/characterisation of smoothness
ideas.modern_name: Relative Kunz theorem (smooth ⇔ flat with flat relative Frobenius)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kunz (1969) absolute case; Radu, André, Dumitrescu (1990s) relative case

deep.surprise_reason: This is a crossed-out list of standing hypotheses for a standard construction (the Cartier operator via the trace of relative Frobenius). The only faint point of interest is that Grothendieck considered flatness of relative Frobenius as the natural hypothesis, which anticipates the relative Kunz viewpoint. But it is undeveloped and abandoned.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads: 'Soit X schéma sur S, tel que X → X^{(p/S)} soit plat et loc. de prés. finie (p.ex. ...'. The last word appears to be 'p.ex.', not 'loc.ex.'.
Line 2: the insertion above the line appears to read roughly 'X → [X^{(p)}] soit [fini?] loc. de prés. finie', relating to F_{X/S}, not to X → S.
Line 4 appears to read 'Ω^1_{X/S} soit loc. libre', ending a clause begun with 'les fibres géométriques'.
The entire box, including the first line, is struck through with horizontal strokes.
